text: Bon is the old religion that began in Tibet, and its followers are called Bonpos.
Bonpos believe it was taught by a Buddha named Tonpa Shenrab and came to Tibet from lands around Mount Kailash.
src: is the indigenous religion of Tibet / Its followers, the Bonpos
Bonpos revere the Buddha Tonpa Shenrab Miwo as its founder / that it came first to the kingdom of Zhangzhung, around Mount Kailash, and then to Tibet

text: Like Buddhists, Bonpos believe in rebirth, being born again after death.
Bon has monks who study holy books and learn to debate.
src: Like Buddhists, Bonpos see the world as a place of suffering and teach karma, rebirth
Bon has celibate monks / who study scripture, train in a debate tradition

text: Bon histories say the Buddhist king Trisong Detsen treated Bon harshly, and its books were hidden as treasures.
Scholars say Bon took its present form more than 900 years ago, when hidden books were brought out again.
src: Bon histories blame the decline of Bon on persecutions under Drigum Tsenpo and the Buddhist king Trisong Detsen / Bon histories say its texts were hidden as treasures
a classical Yungdrung Bon that emerged in the 10th and 11th centuries / bring out Bon texts as Yungdrung Bon takes shape

text: The Fifth Dalai Lama took some Bon monasteries by force, yet he recognised Bon as a Tibetan religion.
Bonpos suffered during an invasion and later in the Cultural Revolution, but their monasteries were allowed to rebuild.
src: The Fifth Dalai Lama converted some Bon monasteries to the Gelug school by force, yet officially recognised Bon as a Tibetan religion
Bon suffered in the Dzungar invasion of 1717 and in the Cultural Revolution / its monasteries were allowed to rebuild after 1980

text: Today about 400,000 Bonpos live on the Tibetan Plateau, the high land of Tibet.
Others follow Bon in the Himalayas, in India and Nepal, and in cities around the world.
src: Scholars estimated about 400,000 followers on the Tibetan Plateau
with communities in the Himalayan regions, India and Nepal and Bonpo centres in cities around the world
